title: the WSG overview of the wilderness - the terrain types, the hierarchy, the bodies of water and the climate zones
audit_comment: The overview of the wilderness, printed pp. 7-10 (pdf 8-11): the seven terrain descriptions (the desert with its 10-inch definition and the 70-foot dune cap, the forest with the cactus-stand exception and the 160-foot temperate maximum, the hills with the 2,000/4,000-foot guideline bands, the mountains with the 4,000-foot minimum and the 10,000/12,000-foot Earth lines, the plains, the seacoast with the encounter-table reclass and the swamp), the 1-through-7 hierarchy of terrain with the highest-wins rule and its two exceptions, the bodies of water and the five climate zones.

banner.title: The WSG OVERVIEW OF THE WILDERNESS, R497: the opening chapter of the book, printed pp. 7-10 (pdf 8-11) - the seven terrain types, the hierarchy of terrain, the bodies of water and the five climate zones. Prose mechanics: no grids, no dice - the load-bearing numbers are the desert rainfall definition, the dune cap, the hills guideline bands, the mountain thresholds and the hierarchy ranking.
banner.provenance: WSG printed pp. 7-10, pdf 8-11, extracted at r497-extraction sha 0d5f109 (tesseract full-text and tsv, x8-x11, 300 dpi, the /tmp-write retry after the empty-shell push 2644f42). The extraction also covers the R498 proficiencies ground: pdf 12-18.

consts.name: wovPrintedLo
consts.comment: the overview chapter starts at printed p. 7.

consts.name: wovPrintedHi
consts.comment: the overview chapter ends at printed p. 10.

consts.name: wovPdfLo
consts.comment: the overview chapter starts at pdf page 8.

consts.name: wovPdfHi
consts.comment: the overview chapter ends at pdf page 11.

consts.name: wovTerrainTypeCount
consts.comment: seven terrain types: desert, forest, hills, mountains, plains, seacoast and swamp.

consts.name: wovClimateZoneCount
consts.comment: five climate zones: arctic, subarctic, temperate, subtropical and tropical.

consts.name: wovHierarchyRankCount
consts.comment: the terrain hierarchy has seven ranks, 1 the highest and 7 the lowest.

consts.name: wovDesertRainMaxIn
consts.comment: the technical definition of a desert: any area receiving less than 10 inches of rain per year.

consts.name: wovDesertTypicalRainIn
consts.comment: most deserts receive half the technical maximum or even less.

consts.name: wovDuneTechnicalMaxFt
consts.comment: a dune is a wind-formed sand accumulation no more than 70 feet high.

consts.name: wovDuneGiantFt
consts.comment: where sand is abundant and the wind very strong, dunes can grow to more than 500 feet high.

consts.name: wovTemperateTreeMaxFt
consts.comment: the largest temperate trees (oak, maple and ash) can reach 160 feet tall.

consts.name: wovHillsLowBandFt
consts.comment: the low hills band: elevation under 2,000 feet with sharply sloping mounds.

consts.name: wovHillsPeaksMayExceedFt
consts.comment: low-band hill peaks may rise above 2,000 feet.

consts.name: wovHillsUpperBandLoFt
consts.comment: the upper hills band starts at 2,000 feet.

consts.name: wovHillsUpperBandHiFt
consts.comment: the upper hills band runs through 4,000 feet.

consts.name: wovMountainMinFt
consts.comment: mountainous terrain usually occurs at 4,000 feet or above.

consts.name: wovEarthTreeLineFt
consts.comment: on Earth the tree line sits at about 10,000 feet above sea level.

consts.name: wovEarthSnowLineFt
consts.comment: beyond the snow line at 12,000 feet trees cannot prosper.

consts.name: wovRankSeacoast
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of seacoast.

consts.name: wovRankSwamp
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of swamp.

consts.name: wovRankForest
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of forest.

consts.name: wovRankPlains
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of plains.

consts.name: wovRankDesert
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of desert.

consts.name: wovRankHills
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of hills.

consts.name: wovRankMountains
consts.comment: the hierarchy rank of mountains.

consts.name: wovHillsGuidelineCount
consts.comment: four classification guidelines govern hilly terrain.

bools.name: wovPolarWastesAreDesert
bools.comment: the icy polar wastes qualify as desert: moisture is abundant as ice but precipitation is very little.

bools.name: wovDesertGravelCommon
bools.comment: most deserts are dry, hard-packed earth beneath a layer of gravel, occasionally broken by large boulders.

bools.name: wovGravelDesertWaterRunsOff
bools.comment: in gravel deserts the rainfall tends to run off the surface instead of soaking in, making water hard to find.

bools.name: wovSandSoaksWater
bools.comment: sand permits water to soak into the terrain, from where it can be recovered later.

bools.name: wovDuneLargerIsDraa
bools.comment: a wind-formed sand accumulation larger than a dune is properly called a sand mountain, or draa.

bools.name: wovDuneWindwardGradual
bools.comment: a dune ascends gradually on the windward side and slopes down sharply on the side opposite the wind.

bools.name: wovDesertBurialRisk
bools.comment: an object remaining in one spot in heavy sand cover may end up buried under tons of sand.

bools.name: wovForestAnyClimateButPolar
bools.comment: forests can be found in any climate except the polar regions.

bools.name: wovCactusStandIsDesert
bools.comment: a large stand of cactus in a desert does not qualify as forest: the area stays desert for weather, food and water determination.

bools.name: wovConifersSubarctic
bools.comment: subarctic forests are evergreens, or conifers.

bools.name: wovDeciduousTemperate
bools.comment: temperate forests are primarily deciduous, leaf-bearing trees.

bools.name: wovRainforestTropical
bools.comment: rainforest is the name for forests in subtropical and tropical climates.

bools.name: wovConiferShedsSnow
bools.comment: the conifer cone shape sheds snow easily; conifer branches are a good source of impromptu shelter material.

bools.name: wovRainforestLayered
bools.comment: the distinctive feature of a rainforest is its layered composition: several tree heights coexisting with low shrubs and ferns.

bools.name: wovRainforestGreenYearRound
bools.comment: rainforest trees are green all year round: new leaves appear before the old ones drop.

bools.name: wovHillsTopographyNotEcology
bools.comment: hills are about topography, not ecology: a forest or a desert can also be hilly.

bools.name: wovHillsDenseTreesAreForest
bools.comment: any irregular terrain with dense or moderate tree cover is forest.

bools.name: wovHillsRollingUnder2000NotHills
bools.comment: gently rolling terrain under 2,000 feet with few or no trees is NOT hills: use desert, plains, swamp or seacoast as appropriate.

bools.name: wovHillsSharpMoundsAreHills
bools.comment: terrain under 2,000 feet with few or no trees and sharply sloping mounds (peaks possibly above 2,000 feet) is hills.

bools.name: wovHillsUpperBandIrregular
bools.comment: terrain between 2,000 and 4,000 feet with irregular ground and few or no trees is hills.

bools.name: wovMountainDevoidOfTrees
bools.comment: mountainous terrain is devoid of large vegetation.

bools.name: wovMountainLowerSlopeTreesAreForest
bools.comment: a heavily wooded area on the lower slopes of a mountain is forest, even above 4,000 feet.

bools.name: wovMountainBeginsWhereTreesEnd
bools.comment: a mountainous region for movement, encounters and food availability begins where the trees end.

bools.name: wovLowRockySlopeCanBeMountain
bools.comment: a barren, rocky slope rising high above the surrounding area can be mountainous even from a base under 4,000 feet.

bools.name: wovAboveSnowLineSnowIce
bools.comment: above the snow line some of the rocky surface is covered with snow or ice, making travel more hazardous.

bools.name: wovExposedRockWarmAir
bools.comment: exposed rock surfaces at high altitude can become much warmer than the air temperature because they absorb the sun heat all day.

bools.name: wovPlainsFlatVegetated
bools.comment: plains are mostly flat, with moderately dense low vegetation except in an arctic climate.

bools.name: wovPlainsTreesNotForest
bools.comment: an occasional tree or small grove on a plain is not enough to qualify as forest.

bools.name: wovPlainsFoodWaterEasy
bools.comment: food and water are generally easy to find on a plain.

bools.name: wovPlainsShelterMaterialScarce
bools.comment: the materials for an impromptu shelter are not easily come by on a plain.

bools.name: wovPlainsSeenFromFarAway
bools.comment: on flat, featureless terrain, characters who can see for a long distance can in turn be seen from far away.

bools.name: wovSeacoastNearOcean
bools.comment: practically any place a short distance from an ocean is seacoast terrain.

bools.name: wovSeacoastDrivesThreeLookups
bools.comment: the seacoast distinction matters for weather conditions, animal availability for food and plant availability for food and medicine.

bools.name: wovSeacoastEncounterReclass
bools.comment: for DMG or Monster Manual II encounter tables, a seacoast area should be treated as the other terrain type that conforms to the table classifications.

bools.name: wovSwampStandingWater
bools.comment: a swamp is any place where a character feet hit standing water shortly before hitting the ground.

bools.name: wovSwampLowElevation
bools.comment: swamps are always located at low elevation or on flat or slightly depressed land at the edge of a river or lake.

bools.name: wovSwampFertileSoil
bools.comment: swamp soil is extremely fertile because it contains a great quantity of decomposed vegetable matter.

bools.name: wovSwampDepthVariesFast
bools.comment: swamp water depth varies from practically zero to several feet, and can go from shallow to deep in a few steps.

bools.name: wovSwampBadForMounts
bools.comment: a swamp is not a good place to take mounts or pack animals.

bools.name: wovHierarchyHighestWins
bools.comment: an area with properties of two or more categories counts as the highest-ranking terrain category.

bools.name: wovBeachIsSeacoast
bools.comment: a sandy beach bordering the ocean is seacoast, not desert.

bools.name: wovWetTreelandIsSwamp
bools.comment: a low-lying area with standing water and a lot of large trees is swamp, not forest.

bools.name: wovOceanRockBaseIsMountains
bools.comment: where ocean waves crash against the base of a jagged rocky slope, the area is mountains, not seacoast.

bools.name: wovMarshValleyIsHills
bools.comment: a marshy area in a deep valley between two hills is hills, not swamp.

bools.name: wovHierarchyLastResort
bools.comment: the ranking is used only when common sense and reasonability do not settle the classification.

bools.name: wovWaterSourceAndChallenge
bools.comment: rivers and lakes provide a ready source of water and require a party to be more versatile: a body of water is both an opportunity and a challenge.

bools.name: wovBoatTravelFasterSafer
bools.comment: travel on a lake or river surface is often faster, easier and safer than the surrounding terrain on foot - but only with a craft and someone skilled to handle it.

bools.name: wovSwimCrossSavesTime
bools.comment: swimming across a deep wide river instead of fording can save hours or even days - but only for characters who can swim.

bools.name: wovPrepareForWater
bools.comment: a party fully prepared for the wilderness carries equipment and skills for coping with bodies of water as well as for moving on land.

bools.name: wovTemperateGreatestExtremes
bools.comment: the greatest extremes of weather from one season to another are found in the temperate zones.

bools.name: wovTemperateEquidistant
bools.comment: the temperate zones lie roughly equidistant from the poles and the equator.

bools.name: wovSubarcticColderDrier
bools.comment: the weather in subarctic regions is usually colder and drier than temperate.

bools.name: wovArcticFrigid
bools.comment: the weather in the arctic zones around each pole is almost always frigid.

bools.name: wovSubtropicalHotter
bools.comment: the subtropical regions have a higher average temperature than the temperate zones.

bools.name: wovSubtropicalPrecipExtremes
bools.comment: subtropical regions show great extremes of precipitation in certain areas from one time of year to the other.

bools.name: wovTropicalWarmExceptHigh
bools.comment: in the tropical zone on either side of the equator the temperature is almost always warm, except at high elevation.

bools.name: wovTropicalHeavyRain
bools.comment: in the tropical zone, precipitation can be extremely heavy in the areas where rain does fall.

bools.name: wovNoBlizzardInTropics
bools.comment: characters will not contend with a raging blizzard in the tropics or a blistering heat wave in the far north, but the weather within a region still travels a wide range.

examples.expr: m['wovPrintedLo']() != 7 or m['wovPrintedHi']() != 10 or m['wovPdfLo']() != 8 or m['wovPdfHi']() != 11

examples.note: the counts: seven terrains, five zones, seven ranks
the desert rainfall: half the technical maximum is typical
examples.expr: m['wovDesertRainMaxIn']() != 10 or m['wovDesertTypicalRainIn']() != 5 or m['wovDesertTypicalRainIn']() * 2 != m['wovDesertRainMaxIn']()

examples.note: the dune split: 70-foot technical cap, 500-foot giants
examples.expr: m['wovDuneTechnicalMaxFt']() != 70 or m['wovDuneGiantFt']() != 500 or m['wovDuneGiantFt']() <= m['wovDuneTechnicalMaxFt']()

examples.note: the hills bands are contiguous: the upper band starts at the low band boundary
the mountain minimum sits at the top of the upper hills band
the Earth tree line is below the snow line
examples.expr: m['wovEarthTreeLineFt']() != 10000 or m['wovEarthSnowLineFt']() != 12000 or m['wovEarthSnowLineFt']() <= m['wovEarthTreeLineFt']()

examples.note: the hierarchy ranks run 1 through 7 with seacoast highest and mountains lowest
examples.expr: m['wovRankSeacoast']() != 1 or m['wovRankSwamp']() != 2 or m['wovRankForest']() != 3 or m['wovRankPlains']() != 4 or m['wovRankDesert']() != 5 or m['wovRankHills']() != 6 or m['wovRankMountains']() != 7

examples.note: the rank ladder sums to 28 and spans six steps
examples.expr: m['wovRankSeacoast']() + m['wovRankSwamp']() + m['wovRankForest']() + m['wovRankPlains']() + m['wovRankDesert']() + m['wovRankHills']() + m['wovRankMountains']() != 28 or m['wovRankMountains']() - m['wovRankSeacoast']() != 6
